description: Assessments that hold up in the exam room and at moderation: an exam paper and its mark scheme checked by a script for totals that don't add up, either/or questions worth different marks, numbering that skips, parts the scheme misses or marks differently, and objectives off their weighting, then read for wording and fairness.

prerequisites: Your exam paper and mark scheme as Word, Markdown or text files
Python 3 on the machine, which the check runs on
first-value.starter-task: Check a test and its mark scheme before printing
first-value.starter-prompt: Check my end-of-unit test (paper.docx) and its mark scheme (mark-scheme.docx) before I print it. Our grid is AO1 40%, AO2 40%, AO3 20%.
first-value.verification: exam-paper-check leads with what to fix before printing, gives each question's marks against its stated total and the paper's, lines the mark scheme up against the paper part by part, and shows marks per objective against your grid.
first-value.recovery: If exam-paper-check does not activate, ask for it by name ("use exam-paper-check"). If your paper is a PDF, save it as Word or text first.

journey.when: A test, mock or assessment is written and about to go to print or to a colleague.
you_bring: your planning grid or objective weightings, if you have them

steps.you_do: Give it the paper, the mark scheme and your weightings.
steps.you_get: What to fix before printing, the marks table, every scheme mismatch, the balance across objectives and wording problems.
steps.decide: Fix and print, or ask for corrected copies.

steps.you_get: The paper and scheme corrected beside your originals, with every change listed.

journey.you_end_with: A paper and mark scheme that add up and match, ready to print or moderate.
